reason: E1 states that friction stir welding of CrCoFeMnNi HEA has been successfully performed, supporting the weldability premise, but it provides no evidence on hot-cracking avoidance, recrystallization quality, or mechanical property superiority of friction stir repair over fusion repair. E2 is about laser cladding of die steel and is irrelevant to the hypothesis. Thus, most key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Friction stir repair avoids hot cracking by staying below the melting point
Friction stir repair produces a fine, dynamically recrystallized, defect-free stir zone
Friction stir repair yields superior mechanical properties vs. fusion-weld repair
High-entropy alloys (e.g., CrCoFeMnNi) are successfully weldable by friction stir welding
